title: Velocity-tiered credits prototype for embeddings & rerank — pricing experiment + QSA intake
creator: Sofia Rinaldi
description:
Summary: Propose a velocity-tiered credit model for embeddings and reranking ('velocity-tiering' meaning discounts that increase with sustained request throughput across a rolling window). Goal is to preserve revenue per unit at baseline while offering better marginal economics to high-throughput customers and smoothing burst behavior to reduce tail GPU pressure.

Why this is different: Existing approaches we’ve evaluated focus on flat per-vector pricing, time-decayed microcredits, or fixed batch-slot models. Velocity-tiering combines per-vector metering with a rolling throughput multiplier that grows with stable daily/hourly vector velocity, capped by slabs, and with a fallback penalty for rapid drop-offs. This is intended to: (1) reward predictable sustained usage, (2) discourage rapid, inefficient bursts that harm cluster packing, and (3) simplify commercial conversations (customers can predict effective price bands based on steady-state velocity).

Hypotheses: 
- H1: For top 30% of customers (by current vector volume), offering a velocity-tiered discount will increase committed spend by >= 8% over 90 days.
- H2: Average GPU tail utilization (99th percentile token latencies during peak windows) will decrease by >= 6% due to smoother arrival patterns.
- H3: Churn risk among mid-market accounts will remain neutral if effective price at observed velocity is <= current per-vector invoice.

Prototype mechanics (engineer-facing):
- Metering: base per-vector unit (PVU) recorded as we do now. Additionally, compute a rolling velocity metric: 1-hour EWMA and 24-hour median of PVU/s.
- Tiers: 3 tiers (Steady, Growth, Scale) triggered when 24-hour median PVU/s crosses thresholds (T1=100k/day, T2=1M/day). Each tier multiplies an effective discount: Steady=0% (base), Growth=10%, Scale=20%. Caps: discounts only apply to sustained volume above the tier threshold and are retroactive within a rolling 24h window.
- Slab cap & decay: Credits persist for up to 72 hours with linear decay if velocity drops; protects revenue when customers burst then drain.
- Billing implications: invoice line-items will include (a) Raw PVU count, (b) Tier-qualified PVU count, (c) Effective discount applied. Clear telemetry will show effective USD/PVU per customer.

Experiment plan: Two-arm experiment for 12 weeks: control (existing per-vector pricing) vs velocity-tiered pilot. Target 120 eligible accounts (selected by historical volatility and ARR). Primary signals: effective $/PVU, net spend delta, churn signals, infra metrics (tail latency, batch efficiency). Secondary signals: support tickets about billing, legal pushback on contract language.

QSA / Enterprise Contract work (intake notes):
- Expose the following to Legal/QSA: tier definitions, measurement window, decay rules, and data retention for metering.
- Proposed contractual language (shortform): 'Customer shall be billed per vector unit consumed. Customer may qualify for velocity-tier discounts when their rolling 24-hour median vector throughput exceeds the published threshold. Discounts are applied retroactively within the applicable measurement window and subject to decay rules as described in the Billing Supplement.'
- QSA checklist items to validate: meter integrity (non-repudiation), audit logs for tier transitions, customer-visible reporting, and KMS-protected billing export.

Success criteria for pilot: 
- Revenue-neutral baseline after prorated adjustments (net uplift target +5% ARR across pilot cohort).
- Backend/serving improvements: 6% reduction in peak 99th latencies for affected clusters.
- Legal: QSA sign-off on draft contract language and billing audit process with no blocking concerns.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: Customers will be confused by retroactive discounts and raise billing disputes. Mitigation: ship preview invoices and a 24-hour tier dashboard in Console before first invoice.
- Risk: Gaming the meter with spikes around threshold windows. Mitigation: use 24-hour median and EWMA, add minimum session duration to qualify for credits.
- Risk: Legal/QSA may require longer retention or stronger non-repudiation. Mitigation: prepare audit logs export and signed metering attestations.

Operational rollout: 
- Phase 0 (Engineering experiment, 2 weeks): implement telemetry, tier calc, preview UI.
- Phase 1 (Pilot, 12 weeks): invite 60 accounts to control/pilot split; show preview invoices; gather feedback.
- Phase 2 (Canary rollout, 4 weeks): enable for managed Dedicated customers with opt-out.
- Phase 3 (Public launch): GA pricing page + updated contract template.

Telemetry & dashboards required: per-customer PVU time series, rolling tier state, effective $/PVU, chargeback reconciliation, and support ticket tagging for billing-related issues.
